readings.subsection: The Reign of Athaliah in Judah
readings.title: Athaliah's Bloody Coup
readings.subtitle: The infant Joash is hidden from the queen's murderous rage.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:1] And Athalyah was the mother of Aḥazyahu. And when she saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all <dn>את</dn> the offspring of the reign. [2] But Yehosheḇa, the daughter of Sovereign Yoram, sister of Aḥazyahu, took <dn>את</dn> Yo’ash son of Aḥazyah, and stole him away from among the sons of the sovereign’s sons who were put to death. So they hid him and his nurse in the bedroom, from Athalyahu, and he was not put to death. [3] And he remained with her in hiding in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for six years, while Athalyah was reigning over the land.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Athaliah in Judah
readings.title: Jehoiada's Counter-Coup
readings.subtitle: The priest organizes the temple guard to anoint the rightful heir.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:4] And in the seventh year Yehoyaḏa sent and brought <dn>את</dn> the commanders of hundreds, with the Karites and the runners, and brought them into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to him. And he made a covenant with <dn>את</dn> them and took an oath from them in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and showed them <dn>את</dn> the son of the sovereign. [5] And he commanded them, saying, “This is what you are to do: One-third of you who come in on the Sabbath to be on guard in the sovereign’s house, [6] and one-third at the gate of Sur, and one-third at the gate behind the runners. And you shall be on guard in the house, lest it be broken down. [7] “And the two detachments of you who are going out on the Sabbath shall be on guard in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the sovereign. [8] “And you shall surround the sovereign on all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand. And whoever comes within the ranks, let him be put to death. And be with the sovereign as he goes out and as he comes in.” [9] So the commanders of the hundreds did according to all that Yehoyaḏa the priest commanded. And each of them took <dn>את</dn> his men who were going in on the Sabbath, with those who were going out on the Sabbath, and came to Yehoyaḏa the priest. [10] And the priest gave the commanders of hundreds <dn>את</dn> the spears and <dn>את</dn> shields which had belonged to Sovereign Daviḏ, that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] And the runners stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, all around the sovereign, from the right side of the House to the left side of the House, by the slaughter-place and the House. [12] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the son of the sovereign and put on him <dn>את</dn> the diadem and <dn>את</dn> the Witness. And they set him up to reign and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, “Let the sovereign live!”

readings.subsection: The Reign of Athaliah in Judah
readings.title: The Usurper's Demise
readings.subtitle: Athaliah is executed as Joash is acclaimed by the people.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:13] And Athalyah heard the noise of the runners, the people, and she came to the people, into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [14] and looked and saw the sovereign standing by a column, according to the ruling, and the chiefs and the trumpeters were beside the sovereign, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. And Athalyah tore her garments and cried out, “Treason! Treason!” [15] And Yehoyaḏa the priest commanded <dn>את</dn> the commanders of the hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, “Take her outside the ranks, and slay with the sword <dn>את</dn> whoever follows her.” For the priest had said, “Do not let her be killed in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [16] So they took hold of her, and she went by way of the horses’ entrance to the sovereign’s house, and was put to death there.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Joash in Judah
readings.title: Covenant and Cleansing
readings.subtitle: Jehoiada leads the people to renew their covenant and purge Baal worship from the land.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:17] And Yehoyaḏa made <dn>את</dn> a covenant between <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the sovereign and the people, to be the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – also between the sovereign and the people. [18] And all the people of the land went to the house of Ba‛al, and broke it down. They completely broke up <dn>את</dn> its slaughter-places and <dn>את</dn> images, and killed <dn>את</dn> Mattan the priest of Ba‛al before the slaughter-places. And the priest appointed inspectors over the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [19] and took <dn>את</dn> the commanders of hundreds, and <dn>את</dn> the Karites, and <dn>את</dn> the runners, and <dn>את</dn> all the people of the land. And they brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign down from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and went by way of the gate of the runners to the sovereign’s house. And he sat on the throne of the sovereigns. [20] And all the people of the land rejoiced. And the city had rest, for they had slain <dn>את</dn> Athalyahu with the sword in the sovereign’s house. [21] Yeho’ash was seven years old when he began to reign.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Joash in Judah
readings.title: Restoration of the House of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: King Joash institutes a plan to fund and complete the temple repairs.
readings.text: [2 Kings 12:1] Yeho’ash began to reign in the seventh year of Yěhu, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Tsiḇyah of Be’ěrsheḇa. [2] And Yeho’ash did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days in which Yehoyaḏa the priest instructed him. [3] However, the high places were not taken away; the people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. [4] And Yeho’ash said to the priests, “All the silver of the set-apart gifts that are brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the silver coming over, each man’s assessment silver, all the silver that a man purposes in his heart to bring into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [5] let the priests take for themselves, each from his friend. And let them strengthen <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House, wherever there is a breach.” [6] And it came to be, by the twenty-third year of Sovereign Yeho’ash, that the priests had not strengthened <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House, [7] and Sovereign Yeho’ash called Yehoyaḏa the priest and the other priests, and said to them, “Why have you not strengthened the breaches of the House? And now, do not take any more silver from your friends, but give it for the breaches of the House.” [8] And the priests agreed that they would neither receive any more silver from the people, nor strengthen <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House. [9] And Yehoyaḏa the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the slaughter-place, on the right side as one comes into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the priests who guarded the door put there <dn>את</dn> all the silver that was brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] And it came to be, whenever they saw that there was much silver in the chest, that the sovereign’s scribe and the high priest came up and put it in bags, and counted <dn>את</dn> the silver that was found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [11] and gave <dn>את</dn> the silver, weighed out, into the hands of those who did the work, who had the oversight of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [12] and to stonemasons and stonecutters, and for buying timber and hewn stone to strengthen <dn>את</dn> the breach of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and for all that was paid out to strengthen the House. [13] However there were not made for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> basins of silver, snuffers, sprinkling-bowls, trumpets, any objects of gold, or objects of silver, from the silver that was brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [14] for they gave that to the workmen, and they strengthened the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with it. [15] And they did not reckon with <dn>את</dn> the men into whose hand they gave <dn>את</dn> the silver to be paid to workmen, for they acted trustworthily. [16] The silver from the trespass offerings and the silver from the sin offerings was not brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It belonged to the priests.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Jehu in Israel
readings.title: The Fading Reign of Jehu
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH begins to diminish Israel's territory during Jehu's final years.
readings.text: [2 Kings 10:32] In those days <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began to cut off some in Yisra’ěl. And Ḥaza’ěl struck them throughout all the border of Yisra’ěl, [33] from the Yarděn to the sun-rising: all <dn>את</dn> the land of Gil‛aḏ – the Gaḏites, and the Re’uḇěnites, and the Menashshehites – from Aro‛ěr, which is by the wadi Arnon, including Gil‛aḏ and Bashan. [34] And the rest of the acts of Yěhu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [35] So Yěhu slept with <dn>את</dn> his fathers, and they buried him in Shomeron. And Yeho’aḥaz his son reigned in his place. [36] And the days that Yěhu reigned over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron were twenty-eight years.
